title: Equivariant clopen trivialization of a finite etale torsor from a section
statement:
Let $U$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $G$ be a finite group, and let $\pi:P\to U$ be a finite etale $G$-torsor with left action, meaning that the action is over $U$ and simply transitive on every geometric fibre [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Suppose $s:U\to P$ is a section, $\pi\circ s=\mathrm{id}_U$. For $g\in G$ put $s_g=g\cdot s$. Then $s_g$ identifies $U$ with an open and closed subscheme $Q_g\subseteq P$, the $Q_g$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $P$, and their inverse maps are $\pi|_{Q_g}$. The morphism
$$\theta:\coprod_{g\in G}U\longrightarrow P,\qquad \theta|_{U_g}=s_g,$$
where the coproduct is the scheme coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], is an isomorphism over $U$. Its inverse is obtained by gluing $\pi|_{Q_g}$ followed by the $g$-indexed coprojection on that disjoint open cover. Moreover $\theta$ is equivariant for the left regular action on its source: for every $h,g\in G$,
$$h\cdot s_g=s_{hg},\qquad h\circ\theta\circ\iota_g=\theta\circ\iota_{hg}.$$
Thus $\theta^{-1}$ is an equivariant trivialization. Empty $U$, disconnected $P$, and the trivial group are allowed.

proof.text: Write $a_g:P\to P$ for the automorphism given by $g$. The action is over $U$, so $\pi s_g=\pi a_gs=\pi s=1_U$ for every $g$. The finite-morphism lemma gives that $\pi$ is separated. Apply the etale separated section lemma to each section $s_g$: it identifies $U$ with the open and closed subscheme $Q_g=s_g(U)$ of $P$, and its inverse is $r_g=\pi|_{Q_g}$. In particular this gives an isomorphism $\bar s_g:U\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_g$ with $\bar s_g r_g=1_{Q_g}$ and $r_g\bar s_g=1_U$.

source.place: Tag 024T, proposition-properties-sections; separatedness from Morphisms Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper

proof.text: The opens $Q_g$ are pairwise disjoint. Indeed, suppose $x\in Q_g\cap Q_h$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(x)$; the residue-field description of geometric points gives $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ over $x$. It factors through both open subschemes. Set $\bar u=\pi\bar x$. Since $r_g$ and $r_h$ are the restrictions of $\pi$ and are inverse to the sections onto their images, these factorizations give equalities of morphisms $\bar x=s_g\bar u=s_h\bar u$. Thus $a_g(s\bar u)=a_h(s\bar u)$ as points of the geometric fibre over $\bar u$, and freeness of that action gives $g=h$. For distinct indices the intersection is therefore the empty open subscheme, not merely a set of distinct rational points.

source.place: Tag 03PO, definition-geometric-point; Schemes Tag 01J9 for the residue-field description; direct use of the torsor hypothesis

proof.text: These opens cover $P$. For any $x\in P$, choose a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ over $x$ by taking an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$ as above, and put $\bar u=\pi\bar x$. Transitivity in the geometric fibre over $\bar u$ supplies $g\in G$ with $\bar x=a_g(s\bar u)=s_g\bar u$. Passing to the image point shows $x\in Q_g$. Hence $P=\bigcup_g Q_g$; this uses geometric points solely to prove an equality of open subsets, not to infer equality of arbitrary scheme morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03PO, definition-geometric-point; Schemes Tag 01J9; direct use of transitivity in the stated hypothesis

proof.text: Form theta = Sigma.desc(s_g). Apply Mathlib isOpenImmersion_sigmaDesc to the disjoint open immersions s_g. Step 3 shows that every point is in the range of theta (use the corresponding coprojection). Hence isIso_of_isOpenImmersion_of_opensRange_eq_top gives an isomorphism. This packages the disjoint-open gluing construction from Stacks Tags 01JB and 01JC, with no separate invocation of general morphism gluing.

proof.text: The coprojection equations for theta and the section equations give theta followed by pi equal to the coproduct projection. For each g, cancel the epimorphism e_g.hom in the proposed inverse restriction: its left side becomes s_g followed by theta.inv, the g-th coprojection; its right side becomes that same coprojection because s_g followed by pi is the identity. This proves the local inverse formula and identifies theta.inv with the gluing of the prescribed restrictions. Its equation over U follows from theta.inv followed by theta.hom being the identity.

source.place: Tags 01JB and 01JC, coproduct mapping property; elementary cancellation in the constructed isomorphisms

proof.text: For $h\in G$ define $L_h:C\to C$ by $L_h\iota_g=\iota_{hg}$. The coproduct universal property and the group law give $L_1=1_C$ and $L_hL_k=L_{hk}$, so these are the left regular action. The action law on $P$ gives $a_hs_g=a_ha_gs=a_{hg}s=s_{hg}$ as scheme morphisms. Consequently $a_h\theta\iota_g=\theta\iota_{hg}=\theta L_h\iota_g$ for every $g$, so coproduct uniqueness gives $a_h\theta=\theta L_h$. Composing this equation with $t$ on both sides gives $t a_h=L_h t$, the requested equivariance of the inverse. If $U$ is empty, the existence of $\pi:P\to U$ forces $P$ empty and all constructions are the unique maps between empty schemes. If $G$ is trivial, its sole section covers $P$ by step 3. No connectedness, reducedness, Noetherian or nonemptiness hypothesis was used.
